question: This phrase is a gender-swapped riff on a catchphrase that comedian Brandon Wardell spread in a July 2016 Vine alongside actor Danny Trejo. Its subject was a 17-year-old western lowland gorilla shot on May 28, 2016, after a three-year-old boy fell into his enclosure. The Cincinnati Zoo, where that incident happened, deleted its Twitter account amid the flood of jokes about him. For 10 points, name this rallying cry urging women to bare their chests in tribute to the slain gorilla.
answer: tits out for Harambe [prompt on Harambe; do not accept or prompt on “dicks out for Harambe”]

question: Rolling Stone profiled the comedian behind this phrase as the voice of a generation. His Vine of it, filmed with Danny Trejo and posted on July 6, 2016, passed two million loops within five days. Trejo had heard the bit at one of the comedian's shows and asked to borrow it. It honors a Cincinnati Zoo gorilla killed in May 2016 after a young boy entered his enclosure. For 10 points, name this crude slogan urging men to expose themselves in tribute to the dead ape.
answer: dicks out for Harambe [prompt on Harambe; do not accept or prompt on “tits out for Harambe”]

question: Editor Jeff Ford suggested the reply to this line late in production, after the directors decided the hero had to say something. That reply called back to the closing words of the 2008 film that launched the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Its speaker snaps his fingers only to find that the stones have been taken from his gauntlet. For 10 points, name this three-word boast by Thanos in Avengers: Endgame, answered by Tony Stark's final declaration.
answer: I am inevitable [or I'm inevitable]

question: The American Film Institute ranked this line second on its 2005 list of the hundred greatest movie quotes, behind only a Gone with the Wind farewell. Its speaker makes the promise after his godson Johnny Fontane asks for help landing a film role that a producer has denied him. That producer later wakes up to find the severed head of his prized horse in his bed. For 10 points, name this line in which Marlon Brando's Vito Corleone vows to present a proposal that cannot be turned down.
answer: I'm gonna make him an offer he can't refuse [or I'm gonna make him an offer he can't refuse; or offer he cannot refuse]

question: Peter Jackson revealed that the actor delivering this line had the speech taped to his knee, because it was rewritten the night before filming. That explains why the speaker keeps glancing downward during the Council of Elrond. Its image macro, which swaps the ending for any difficult task, peaked in popularity around early 2012. For 10 points, name this line in which Sean Bean's Boromir warns that entering Sauron's realm is no easy stroll, in The Fellowship of the Ring.
answer: One does not simply walk into Mordor [or One does not simply]

question: The caption of this image macro adapts the motto of a noble house whose seat is Winterfell. Its second half is swapped out to warn of any imminent flood, such as exam results, spoilers or holiday advertising. The image shows Sean Bean in furs as Eddard Stark in the first season of HBO's Game of Thrones. For 10 points, name this meme whose caption tells viewers to prepare for the arrival of the coldest season.
answer: Brace yourselves, winter is coming [or Brace yourself; prompt on winter is coming]

question: Its speaker says this line on a bridge over a vast shaft in Starkiller Base, moments before running a lightsaber through his father. He tells Han Solo he is being torn apart and wants to be free of the pain, then asks for help. Reaction images of it ironically caption trivial temptations like a second dessert or skipping class. For 10 points, name this confession of resolve undercut by self-doubt, spoken by Kylo Ren in Star Wars: The Force Awakens.
answer: I know what I have to do but I don't know if I have the strength to do it [or I don't know if I have the strength to do it]

question: This remark comes from the second episode, “Cult of Personality”, of a 2020 Netflix docuseries. Its speaker said it on learning that a tiger had torn off an employee's arm at his park in Wynnewood, Oklahoma. Clips of it went viral from March 20, 2020, when the series premiered during early COVID-19 lockdowns. For 10 points, name this lament by Joe Exotic in Tiger King, now used as a reaction to any purchase that drains the wallet.
answer: I am never going to financially recover from this [or I'm never gonna financially recover from this; or never going to financially recover]

question: The most-viewed remix of this clip claimed to repeat it 1,073,741,824 times, or two to the thirtieth power. YouTube user Boredmations2 posted the clip on November 10, 2016, amid a wave of edits of its source film. It is the awkward opener a bee uses on florist Vanessa Bloome after she saves him from being squashed. For 10 points, name this question about a musical genre asked by Barry B. Benson in the 2007 DreamWorks film Bee Movie.
answer: Ya like jazz [or You like jazz; or Do you like jazz]

question: Tumblr user kidpix2 first paired this caption with a photo of a Budgett's frog in a December 2014 post. Vine creator Jimmy Here popularized it by saying the phrase and then imitating the frog's scream. It resurfaces across the internet every week, but only on one specific day. For 10 points, give this catchphrase announcing to one's pals that it is hump day.
answer: It is Wednesday, my dudes [or It's Wednesday my dudes]

question: Around 2017, fandoms on Tumblr adopted this phrase to mock stories that pass off obvious couples as merely platonic housemates. The original Vine was uploaded by @mattsukkar on October 25, 2014, and had been played over 67 million times by 2018. In it, the uploader films a woman walking past while talking on her phone, then repeats her words in an exaggerated gasp. For 10 points, name this Vine punchline about two people sharing an apartment.
answer: And they were roommates [or Oh my god, they were roommates]

question: Paul Lieberstein wrote and directed the episode whose cold open centers on this activity, which aired on September 17, 2009. In that scene, Andy Bernard hurts himself by jumping onto a refrigerator box that turns out to be empty. The participants hop over desks and boxes while mostly just shouting the activity's name. For 10 points, name this obstacle-course discipline that Michael, Dwight and Andy attempt in the season six premiere of The Office.
answer: Parkour

question: Its speaker shouted this line twice from his seat during the presentation of the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature. It followed a G.I. Jane joke about Jada Pinkett Smith, who has alopecia. The next day its speaker apologized, admitting he had been out of line. For 10 points, name this profane demand Will Smith yelled at Chris Rock after slapping him at the 2022 Oscars.
answer: Keep my wife's name out your fucking mouth [or Keep my wife's name out of your fucking mouth; or Keep my wife's name out your mouth]

question: Posters hoping for this outcome announce a GET attempt, a practice borrowed from Japanese imageboards. It is the step above trips and the step below quints. A 4chan post numbered 12345555 would earn this label for the run at its end. For 10 points, name this 4chan slang for a post number ending in four identical digits.
answer: quads [or quadruples; or quadruple digits]

question: The Bibliotheca Anonoma wiki describes these users as clueless, overeager former lurkers who make their presence obvious. They are typically scolded with “lurk moar”, a misspelled instruction to read longer before posting. The opposite label goes to users who have browsed since 4chan's first years. For 10 points, name this crude 4chan compound for a newbie, the counterpart of an oldfag.
answer: newfag [or newfags]

question: In 2013, a 4chan user nicknamed prime minister face found a Turkish cupcake brand with this name, since its second syllable means cake in Turkish. Its root spread through World of Warcraft, where Horde players typing lol appear to Alliance players to type a different three-letter word. That root was later tied to a frog-headed Egyptian god of darkness and to Pepe the Frog. For 10 points, name this 4chan slang for the best possible laugh.
answer: topkek [or top kek]

question: Christopher Poole chose this default name as the English version of the Japanese label Futaba Channel gave its users, which translates as nameless. Because everyone who leaves the Name field blank posts under it, 4chan culture treats it as a hive collective rather than one person. A hacktivist collective that grew out of the site took this name. For 10 points, give this label, often shortened to four letters, that 4chan shows for a poster who enters no name.
answer: Anonymous [or Anon]

question: When Christopher Poole launched 4chan at age 15 in 2003, this board was among the first, originally sharing its name with anime. Its near-total lack of rules made it the most notorious board on the site and the source of countless early memes and raids. Its name is written as one lowercase letter between two slashes. For 10 points, name this 4chan board for miscellaneous, off-topic posting.
answer: /b/ [or b; or Random]

question: Peter Morley-Souter, drawing as TangoStari, coined this phrase in an August 13, 2003 webcomic about his shock at finding adult parodies of Calvin and Hobbes. It was later included in a tongue-in-cheek list of internet laws compiled on 4chan. It holds that if something exists, explicit content of it exists too, with no exceptions. For 10 points, name this numbered internet maxim.
answer: Rule 34 [or Rule thirty-four; or Rule #34]

question: The photo behind this caption was posted on February 13, 2010, by Japanese kindergarten teacher Atsuko Sato. Its subject, a rescued dog named Kabosu, died in May 2024 at age 18. Captions like it scatter broken phrases built on words like very and so in multicolored Comic Sans. For 10 points, give this ungrammatical caption praising a side-eyeing Shiba Inu as chill and amazing, the model for many others in its meme.
answer: such cool much wow [or much wow such cool; prompt on Doge]

question: This material's meme fame began with a December 2023 video by TikTok account @homedesign369 about remodeling a child's bedroom. The Unhinged Home Design videos that feature it propose absurd expansions of tiny rooms. It is used to cover the frame the narrator builds from galvanized square steel. For 10 points, name this environmentally conscious thin wooden surface that finishes nearly every renovation in the meme.
answer: eco-friendly wood veneers [or eco friendly wood veneers; or eco-friendly wood veneer; prompt on wood veneers]

question: In absurd home renovation TikToks, these items anchor the galvanized square steel used to enlarge rooms of about 1.8 square meters. The running joke took off on TikTok and Reddit in May 2024 as users added them to every other video. They are specifically expansion fasteners rather than nails or bolts. For 10 points, name this hardware the narrator borrows from a parent's sister.
answer: screws from your aunt [or expansion screws borrowed from your aunt; or screws borrowed from your aunt; or screws from aunt]

question: Merriam-Webster added this word in September 2023, dating its first known use to 2013. Its second half ironically grants nobility or a villain's rank to the person it describes. Its first half comes from calling provocative content cutting or daring. For 10 points, name this term for someone who makes wildly dark, exaggerated statements online to shock others.
answer: edgelord [or edge lord]

question: The practice this tallies was promoted by a British orthodontist as part of a theory called orthotropics. That practice involves pressing the tongue flat against the roof of the mouth to sculpt a sharper jawline. One TikTok commenter thanked the orthodontist for a two-year one. For 10 points, name this looksmaxxing count of how long someone has kept up that tongue posture without breaking it.
answer: mewing streak [prompt on mewing]

question: A viral parody asks whether someone has ever been on one of these, spoofing the rapid-fire interlinked baseline test from Blade Runner 2049. Reaction GIFs mourn a character who has just lost one. It counts how long someone has held off from finishing while pleasuring themselves. For 10 points, name this tally of delayed climax, a close cousin of the No Nut November challenge.
answer: edging streak [or edge streak; prompt on edging; do not accept or prompt on “gooning streak”]

question: Urban Dictionary's earliest definition of the root activity, added on August 18, 2005, described a man becoming a total dimwit from self-pleasure. Communities devoted to that activity formalized on Reddit in 2019, and memes about dedicated caves and kits spread from late 2022. In brainrot slang the activity can also mean being obsessively consumed by a game or trend. For 10 points, name this tally of consecutive days spent in trance-like marathon sessions of adult content.
answer: gooning streak [or goon streak; prompt on gooning; do not accept or prompt on “edging streak”]
